note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent judge, authored none of the Section 7.3 fragment-selector fix). Section 7.3: "However, a receiver MUST discard non-initial fragments that arrive on an SA with non-trivial port (or ICMP type/code or MH type) selector values unless this feature has been negotiated." Ze negotiates no NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO, so every Child SA with a non-trivial selector must refuse non-initial fragments. Kernel boundary read in Linux 7.3: __xfrm_decode_session memsets the keys and dissects with FLOW_DISSECTOR_F_STOP_AT_ENCAP only (no PARSE_1ST_FRAG); __skb_flow_dissect ends at OUT_GOOD for an IPv4 fragment and for an IPv6 fragment header, and `if (!(key_control->flags & FLOW_DIS_IS_FRAGMENT))` guards __skb_flow_dissect_ports, while ip_proto is still recorded; decode_session4/6 copy the zeroed ports and ICMP type/code; ip_forward and ip6_forward run the FWD policy check and the route lookup with no defragmentation of their own. So a fragment presents (proto, 0, 0): an exact non-zero port or ICMP type/code selector misses it and the decapsulated packet meets XfrmInNoPols (secpath_has_nontransport), while an exact 0 matches it. The prior FINDING is closed for every producer read: programmableSelector (ts_narrow.go) now refuses portMatchesEveryFragment (PortSingle with Port 0, which under ICMP/ICMPv6 is type 0 code 0), and it is the gate of both narrowSelectors (responder) and answerPairs (initiator); wireToSelectors drops a range starting at 0 rather than narrowing it to 0; configured selectors refuse port 0 at parse; PortSelector has no masked-block form, and selectorPort emits only ANY or exact; childPolicyPair (child.go) applies the same predicate to both halves before any PROTECT policy is built, so a rekey floor (floorWithinProposal answers floor pairs without programmablePair) or an inherited selector set cannot install one either; icmpSelectorFromIKE is reached only through childPolicyPair. Units: positive TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryCarriesSelectorDirectionOrderAndTemplate (inbound entry keeps exact port 443, red if widened to ANY); negative TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryIsRefusedRatherThanWidened (inbound and outbound ports with a bit outside the mask, 443 and 0x0100 under 0x00ff, refused; claim matches body); negative TestNarrowingRefusesASelectorEveryFragmentMatches (a proposed TSi single port 0 under TCP and ICMP type 0 code 0, read from the 0-0 wire pair, make narrowSelectors answer not-ok against no policy and against an any-port policy, while 179, ICMP 0/3, ICMP 8/0 and any port are accepted with one pair whose TSi port is unchanged; isolated, since nothing else in programmableSelector refuses those inputs, and red if the predicate is removed). Claim wording: "accepted unchanged" is wider than the body, which asserts only the pair count and the TSi port; suggest "accepted with the TSi port unchanged". The value is tested on TSi only; TSr runs through the same programmableSelector. The second check (childPolicyPair) is proved by the untagged TestChildPolicyPairRefusesASelectorEveryFragmentMatches. FINDING, residual and outside the selector shape these units judge: every Child SA carries ReqID defaultReqID (1, create_child.go newChildSA, constant in child.go) and its template carries no SPI (dataplane/xfrm_linux.go xfrmPolicyFromParams), and xfrm_state_ok matches a template on proto, reqid, mode and tunnel endpoints only. A non-initial fragment decrypted on Child SA A with exact port selectors is therefore accepted when another Child SA of the same peer (same outer endpoints) installs an any-port FWD policy covering its addresses. The fragment then complies with that policy (7.3-5 holds), but it was not discarded although it arrived on A; this is the per-SA inbound binding the 4.1-9 parallel-SA design relies on, reported to the lead, not a verdict change. Prior judgement: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent judge, authored none of spec-rfc4301-architecture-gaps). Section 7.3: "However, a receiver MUST discard non-initial fragments that arrive on an SA with non-trivial port (or ICMP type/code or MH type) selector values unless this feature has been negotiated." The stale unit TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryIsRefusedRatherThanWidened now refuses an inbound port whose bits lie outside its mask (443 and 0x0100 under 0x00ff), and the 7.3-4 negative claim says exactly that; the positive (inbound entry keeps exact port 443) is unchanged. For an exact non-zero port the judgement stands: Linux reads no ports from a non-initial fragment, so the fragment presents port 0 and misses the selector. FINDING, owed a check, not a verdict change on the tagged scope: this spec made an exact selector value of 0 installable (the carried netlink patch writes explicit masks), so a Child SA negotiated with a single port 0 (a peer's 0-0 narrowed from a local any, ts_narrow.go, PortSelectorFromWire) or with ICMP type 0 code 0 (icmpSelectorFromIKE, child.go) installs a selector a portless non-initial fragment matches; on the forward path, where Linux does not reassemble before the policy check, such a fragment would pass. Not observed by any test and not yet read in the kernel's decode_session4; reported to the lead. Prior judgement: Forbidden: accepting a non-initial fragment on an SA with non-trivial port selectors (Ze has no NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO negotiation). Ze's boundary is the inbound XFRM policy the kernel checks; Linux decodes no ports for a non-initial fragment, so an exact port selector refuses it. TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryCarriesSelectorDirectionOrderAndTemplate asserts in.SrcPort == 443 on the inbound entry, red if the selector is widened to ANY. TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryIsRefusedRatherThanWidened asserts a partial mask (0x00ff) is refused for SADirIn and SADirOut, red if it is installed widened.
